title: A Year on This Planet Lasts Just 5.7 Hours

scenes.text: There's a planet where a whole year lasts 5.7 hours.
It's about Earth's size, and it orbits so close to its star that it's almost being pulled apart.
The star's gravity stretches it into an egg shape, ten percent longer one way.
Its orbit is shrinking. In roughly 400 million years, it could be torn to pieces.
Astronomers who found it in 2024 say it's on the verge of being torn apart.
A year of 5.7 hours. That's shorter than a workday.

description:
A planet called TOI-6255 b, found in 2024, is about the size of Earth and circles its star in just 5.7 hours.
Its orbit sits just outside the point where tides would tear it apart, and astronomers estimate it could reach that point in roughly 400 million years.
If you lived there, how many birthdays would you have by lunchtime?
first_comment: A year of 5.7 hours means about four birthdays a day. How old would you be by now?
